newsitem.title: USA: West TeleServices raising capital spending.
newsitem.headline: West TeleServices raising capital spending.

text.p: West TeleServices Corp said Wednesday it expects to increase capital spending and continue its strong momentum in 1997 after reporting higher fourth quarter and 1996 earnings.
West TeleServices, which provides customized telephone-based services, said it plans capital spending of about $46 million in 1997, up from nearly $36 million in 1996.

"We plan a continuous increase in the number of workstations, the number of interactive ports and the number of call centers and facilities in which we operate," Troy Eaden, chief executive officer, said in a statement.

"We project our capital spending plans for 1997 to be approximately $46 million, primarily for the capacity expansion and upgrades at existing facilities and the addition of five new call centers," he said.

Earlier, West TeleServices reported fourth quarter earnings of $0.12 a share on a proforma basis versus $0.09 last year. Earnings for the year were $0.52 a share versus $0.42. The company held an initial public offering on Novemeber 26, 1996.
The company said the strong results reflect increased demand for outsourced telecommunications-based services to businesses, and "anticipates continuing positive momentum for the coming year".

During the fourth quarter the company added 425 telephone workstations, giving it a total of 4,440 as of December 31, compared with 3,158 at the end of 1995. West has 11 operating facilities located in Nebraska, Texas and Virginia.
